levels.description: A practical scholar whose every thrown vial stings twice. At star one she has no mana to charge - just the acid doing its quiet work on every hit.
Stronger acid, heftier flask. The Volatile Mixture fires when the flask charges full - a bubble of debuffs that soaks an entire cluster in Vulnerability and Slow.
The strongest acid, the widest blast, and a lasting pool of toxic residue that punishes any enemy who tries to walk through the crater. The battlefield map no longer belongs to fast melee units.
A fragrant ball of catnip. Stationary; enemy cats nearby cannot resist attacking it.
A fragrant ball of catnip. Stationary; enemy cats nearby cannot resist attacking it.
A fragrant ball of catnip. Stationary; enemy cats nearby cannot resist attacking it.

The Crown Heir at rank one contributes nothing beyond their physical presence. Place them safely - they are the investment that pays out when the shop upgrades. On level-up it branches into Queen (option 0) or King (option 1) - AI picks at random; player choice UI still pending (/ux-design).
The King at rank two - formation commander. His global Sovereign's Aura passively buffs all Nobles' Armor and Attack Damage; Royal Command surges all stats on mana full.
The Queen at rank two - frontline fighter. Her Vanguard Aura buffs nearby Noble Attack Speed; Sovereign's Charge dashes to the highest-HP enemy and stuns.

The High King at rank three - the ultimate formation multiplier. His global Sovereign's Aura II buffs all Nobles; Royal Command II surges the entire formation; King's Protection grants adjacent Nobles Last Stand once per combat.
The High Queen at rank three - frontline fighter supreme. Her Battle Cry triggers on every kill, driving the Noble formation into a frenzy.
A enchanted grey rat, quick and twitchy.
A very fat, very round rat with sleek grey fur, a smug expression, and a tiny golden crown. Waddles rather than runs.
The Peasants' cheapest frontline.
Fighter hardens up.
Fighter becomes the Village Champion.
She tosses a ball of catnip onto the field; enemy cats around it can't help but attack it.
Sturdier catnip with a wider lure radius.
Two catnip balls may be on the field at once.

The wildcard of the Noble faction \u2014 unpredictable, disruptive, and oddly dangerous for a clown. Distract spreads incoming damage by confusing enemy targeting, keeping the Jester alive longer than its HP suggests. On full mana, Tumble leaps onto the furthest enemy and hops back.
Distract chance raised to 30%. Tumble II now Stuns on landing \u2014 leaping into the enemy backline to Stun clustered enemies and escaping before they can retaliate.

Distract chance 35%. Tumble III: Stun 1.2s, and a kill chains into another leap (up to 3). Passive: every 3rd basic attack randomly grants a nearby ally +15% Attack Speed for 3s \u2014 the Jester becomes a passive support unit even when Tumble is on cooldown.
The cheapest defensive unit in the Nobles roster. Pure stats tank - the reliable frontline anchor that taunts nearby enemies when hit.
Shield Bash gives the Knight offensive pressure. On Mana Full, the Knight stuns the primary target and raises a shield barrier for itself.
Shield Bash II - Stun the primary target (1.5s) and raise a +35 HP Shield. Also stuns all enemies adjacent to the primary target (0.8s, unsupported - adjacency AoE pending engine implementation).
The Peasants' premium tank. When his mana fills, he winds up and spins his axe, dealing AoE damage and knocking back everyone around him.
The Peasants' premium tank. When his mana fills, he winds up and spins his axe, dealing AoE damage and knocking back everyone around him.
The Peasants' premium tank. When his mana fills, he winds up and spins his axe, dealing AoE damage and knocking back everyone around him.
The youngest Academy graduate.
The youngest Academy graduate.
The youngest Academy graduate.
A necromantic scholar of the Arcane Academy. When her mana fills she raises the nearest fallen ally at 25% health - each ally can only be raised once.
A necromantic scholar of the Arcane Academy. When her mana fills she raises the nearest fallen ally at 50% health - each ally can only be raised once.
Raise Dead III restores the fallen ally to full health.

The Arcane Academy's anti-heal specialist. Every attack infects the target with Wound, halting regeneration and rendering healing futile. A single Plague Caster counters an entire sustain composition.
Wound intensifies to \u221250%. Plague Spray fires 5 bolts at random enemies on mana full, spreading Wound instantly across the enemy board and shutting down faction-wide healing simultaneously.

Wound reaches \u221270% for 5s. Each Plague Spray bolt now also applies Vulnerability (+20% damage taken, 3s) - combining no-heal and damage-amplify on every target hit. Paired with a Rat Enchanter, a target receives +60% effective incoming damage.
The core force multiplier of the Peasants. Her aura makes a weak army dangerous just by her presence. Protect her, or let her death echo be plan B.
The core force multiplier of the Peasants. Her aura makes a weak army dangerous just by her presence. Protect her, or let her death echo be plan B.
The core force multiplier of the Peasants. Her aura makes a weak army dangerous just by her presence. Protect her, or let her death echo be plan B.
A scruffy grey field rat, quick and twitchy. No magic - just teeth and bad intentions.
A enchanted grey rat, quick and twitchy.
A very fat, very round rat with sleek grey fur, a smug expression, and a tiny golden crown. Waddles rather than runs.
Vermina, a slight, hooded Academy cat.
Vermina's enchantment deepens. Her summoned Rats become Enchanted Rats.
Vermina summons royalty.
A very fat, very round rat with sleek grey fur, a smug expression, and a tiny golden crown. Waddles rather than runs.
The Nobles' precision ranged unit. Rewards clean positioning behind the Knight frontline with a passive Attack Damage bonus.
Gains Volley at full mana \u2014 fires 3 arrows at 3 different enemies. Precision Shot line-of-sight bonus increases to +20% AD.
Volley fires 5 arrows, each applying Vulnerability. Precision Shot line-of-sight bonus reaches +25% AD \u2014 devastating behind a Knight wall.
A mounted knight who builds speed on the ride in and crashes into the enemy line.
The charge now slows everyone around the impact.
The charge now stuns everyone around the impact.
The Arcane Academy's hard-CC caster. On Mana Full she unleashes Hush, Silencing her target and stripping their ability window entirely.
Hush II extends Silence to 4s and adds a follow-up Stun - the target staggers upon regaining ability access, double CC from a single cast.
Hush III: Silence 5s + immediate Stun 1.5s, and the silenced target takes +20% damage for 5s.
The Nobles' foremost Paladin. A methodical, unshakeable presence who hardens through combat. Heavy tank with no mana at rank one. Steadfast raises his Armor and Magic Resist over time.
Gains Divine Shield on mana full \u2014 Unbreakable for 4s and a +60 HP barrier. Steadfast grants +3 Armor and +2 Magic Resist per stack.
Divine Shield grants Unbreakable for 4s and Shield +100, and Tenacity +10% for 4s to allies within 2.5. Steadfast grants Armor and Magic Resist per stack.
A scrappy alley cat who answers the call for a bowl of leftovers.
A tipsy Tavern recruit. Never sold in the shop.
Wren the Hurler lobs tomeowtos from safe range. Fragile but punishing \u2014 every throw has a 20% chance to Stun the target for 0.5s.
Wren hones her aim. Each throw now slows on hit too, and her stuns land harder. Still fragile - but harder to ignore.
The Giant Tomeowto. Wren launches an oversized tomeowto that stuns all enemies in a small area. Paired with Barrage she can hold an entire flank from across the board.
An ancient cat whose name no one knows. He carries a staff worn smooth from decades of use. His aura of blessing strengthens allies within 5 tiles \u2014 slow to move, impossible to rattle.
He has seen worse. The Elder's blessing now reaches 7 tiles and deepens for every ally within range. He does not hurry. The battle comes to him.
At his strongest the Elder's aura fills the entire field (8 tiles). Those who stand in it do not merely fight harder \u2014 they endure.
A polished oak-and-iron siege crossbow on a swivel mount, dressed in Crown Guard livery. Fires at the highest-HP enemy in range, ignoring a portion of their armour.
Reinforced limbs and heavier bolts. The bolt now pierces through the primary target, striking the first enemy behind them for reduced damage.
Reinforced limbs engraved with gold plate. The heaviest siege crossbow in the Crown Guard arsenal. Every fourth bolt is a Skewer Shot that tears through the target's Max HP.
A heavy timber siege engine with indigo-and-gold Crown Guard banners on its frame and a counterweight stamped with the royal crest. Hurls boulders into dense enemy clusters.
A taller frame with counterweights doubled. Boulders scatter survivors with Knockback on impact, clearing the hit zone.
A towering trebuchet with ceremonial gold fittings and the royal crest on its counterweight. Stuns enemies at the inner impact zone. On destruction, launches one final boulder.
The Peasants' dedicated healing building. Heals the lowest-HP ally on a pulse, keeping the frontline alive.
The Peasants' dedicated healing building. Heals the lowest-HP ally on a pulse, keeping the frontline alive.
The Peasants' dedicated healing building. Heals the lowest-HP ally on a pulse, keeping the frontline alive.
The Milk Tavern drafts Peasant Fighters during combat, giving the Peasants an endless stream of cheap bodies to fill the front row.
Production interval drops by 25%. The first Fighter arrives instantly at combat start, and every spawn briefly gains All Stats \u2014 milk-fuelled and ready for battle.

The Tavern at full production. Two Fighters arrive instantly, the interval halves, and spawns gain permanent All Stats. If the Tavern falls, every Fighter it ever sent surges with Attack Damage as a final gift.

A weathered stone cat-grotesque crouched on a carved plinth. Stationary ward - enemies that enter its aura are slowed. Wakes when an ally dies or it drops to half HP, rising as a Roused Gargoyle for the rest of combat.
The stone cracks and the gargoyle wakes. The Magic Cats' only true frontline tank - slow but heavily armoured. Looming Presence travels with it as a moving ward, slowing enemies who press against it.

Tower-tall, moss-grown and rune-scored. The Grimalkin at full power - when mana fills it unleashes Stone Smash, slamming the ground to damage and knock back all enemies in a 2-tile radius. Looming Presence now reaches 4 tiles.
